$comment: CANDIDATE, 2026-09-06. Not live. Built from his rulings (80 minutes tops, legs first, no solo lifts, four days) and his words on 2026-09-06: supersets to make it shorter, chest in the week, no calf raise, a warm-up he understands, and the app telling him what he did last time.
Every block is a pair. Every partner is a lift he has logged. Every main lift is one he has history on, which the live file could not say of its bench.

goal.his: Get stronger on the main lifts, legs first, with form I trust, while the fat comes off. Stay athletic: jumps and sideways work inside the sessions, a carry in the week, and the swim after every lift.
goal.measuredBy: Working weight on the eight main lifts, read once a month against the month before. Bodyweight and fat come from HealthOS/CURRENT.md and are never restated here. Longest unbroken swim from the lap data.

inHisWords.said: lose weight and try to either increase strength, increase muscle or don't lose as much muscle... increasing strength and loose fat
I don't want to lose track of my main lifts. The squats, the bench, the rows, whatever. We have made progress on that. That has to keep happening.
Working out as an athlete, I think that's what my goal is.
I feel like all this lifting is just one plane. I am not doing side or whatever else.
this whole project started with me wanting to work on my lower body strength and now it seems it has become secondary
I'm more worried on like keeping my form and maybe improving on that than going heavier
I would also want to do stuff for posture ... The swimming ... just evening has the lift before the swim same with walk run

goal.decided: Candidate wording 2026-09-06; the athletic clause moves inside the two sessions because Session C is folded into them. HIS to confirm or change.
assumptions: Bench on the barbell: already the live prescription, moves in 5 lb steps. His call to move back to dumbbells.
FULL version, his choice 2026-09-04 ("1 FULL"): about 85 to 90 minutes a session, past the 80-minute ceiling he set on 2026-08-30. The optional blocks are the ones to drop when short.
Swim in the evening after the lift, his choice 2026-09-04, reversing the 2026-09-03 morning ruling. The swim goal in content/swim/plan.json is re-anchored to one swim rather than the morning slot.
Walk-run after Session B (Tuesday, Friday), before the swim where there is one; the easy row after Session C. The bike is unscheduled, kept as a page.

acceptedGaps.abs: The only direct abdominal work is the hanging knee raise, bodyweight, progressed by reps. Accepted 2026-09-03: he chose it over the dead bug ("I rather do hanging knee raises"), every loadable alternative in the gym has under three logged sets, and the front squat and the RDL load the trunk as a helper on every session. Take this out the day a loadable ab exercise earns six logged rows.

changes.hisWords: I'd rather do supersets with the objective of making this shorter. I don't understand the point of having session a, session b, session c if I don't even know what I did last session. there's barely chest at all. I don't even understand why we need calf raises.
changes.what: Two sessions, every block paired, four lifting days, chest in both, calves gone, jumps and bounds as primers inside A and B, Session C folded in. Warm-up cut to two items plus the ramp.

frozen.$why: Fifty-three commits to this file in twenty-four days and twenty-two reversals. Every one was individually defensible and the week never landed. The gate makes "an agent redesigns the week" unrepresentable until the review date. To change the week before then, add {on, hisWords, hash} to `changes` with his quoted sentence of at least eight words and the new hash from --print-hash. The commit message should carry the same words.

blocks.label: Jump
blocks.why: Three jumps of three between your squat warm-up sets, while you are fresh. Your own ask on 15 August: "working out as an athlete". It is here instead of in a session of its own so the athletic work happens in the session you are already in.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.cue: Three jumps a set, then stop. You are training how fast you leave the floor, and a tired jump is a slow one. Stand a forearm length from the box, swing the arms back, bend the knees a quarter of the way, and jump ONTO the box. Land with both feet flat and knees bent, quietly. STEP down, never jump down. A thud, or a third jump slower than the first, means the box is too high.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

alts.name: Lateral Bound
alts.cue: Three bounds a side, then stop. Stand on your LEFT leg, push off sideways and land on your RIGHT leg only, then FREEZE for two seconds before going back. Land with the knee bent and pointing over the toes, never caving inward. Only jump as far as you can land and hold. Silent landing, no wobble, no second little hop. If you cannot freeze it, go shorter.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces on the balls of your feet, stiff ankles. 3x15.

alts.name: Banded Lateral Walk
alts.cue: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Short band above the knees, seated on a bench. Push the knees apart against the band and hold two seconds at the widest point, then let them come back slowly. Success looks like: you feel it on the outside of the hip, above and behind the hip bone. 3x15.

alts.name: Clamshell
alts.cue: On your side, short band above the knees, knees bent 90. Open the top knee like a clam without letting your hips roll backwards. Success looks like: your top hip stays stacked over the bottom one. If you have to roll back to open further, you have gone as far as it goes. 3x15 each side.

blocks.label: Squat, knee raises in the rest
blocks.why: The heavy squat first, three sets at your own rep range, going up 5 lb when all three sets reach the top. The knee raises ride in its three-minute rest on the bar above the rack, your own pairing from 3 September, and they add no time.

exercises.name: BB Back Squat
exercises.cue: The lift the week is built around. Stance a little wider than your hips, toes turned out slightly. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach as if about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Lighter than the back squat on purpose. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Fingertips just hook under the bar; the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. Because the bar is in front, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier. If the elbows drop the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.cue: Hang from the bar on top of the rack, arms straight, feet clear of the floor. Bring both knees up toward your chest, and at the top keep going a couple of inches by curling your hips under you. That last bit is the part your abdominals do. Lower under control until your legs are straight and you have come to a STOP before the next rep. No swinging. When fifteen is easy, straighten the legs instead of adding weight.

alts.name: Plank w/ Shoulder Taps
alts.cue: On the floor. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, put it back, tap with the other. Success looks like: your hips do not rock side to side as the hand leaves the floor. If they rock, put your feet wider. 3x10 each side.

alts.name: Band Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.

alts.name: Hollow Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

exercises.whyHere: your own pairing from 3 September, and they add no time

blocks.label: Bench, lateral raises in the rest
blocks.why: The barbell bench, the press you asked to keep track of, in the rack while you are still there after the squat. The lateral raises ride in its rest because the dumbbells travel to the rack and the side of the shoulder does nothing in a bench press. The low-incline dumbbell press you have been doing is the first alternative, one tap.

exercises.name: BB Bench Press
exercises.cue: Flat bench inside the rack. Set the safety pins at chest height BEFORE you load the bar, every time, because you train alone. Feet flat, grip a little wider than your shoulders, shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower to your lower chest until it touches lightly, press up, same spot every rep. If you have to bounce it, it is too heavy. Start at 135 and find the weight over two sessions.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat, a dumbbell in each hand. Shoulder blades pulled back and down into the bench and kept there. Lower until you feel a stretch across the chest, pause one second, press up over your lower chest. Your history here is 65 to 75 lb.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: A press on a machine, moderate rather than heavy: the barbell bench is where the press gets pushed. Machine on purpose, so a tired chest does not have to balance dumbbells. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if pouring from two jugs. Lower about twice as slowly as you lifted. Success: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top. If either fails, go lighter.

alts.name: KB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

exercises.whyHere: the side of the shoulder does nothing in a bench press

blocks.label: Row, reverse flies in the rest
blocks.why: The heavy horizontal pull, still at the rack. The reverse flies ride in its rest because they travel and they are the back-of-the-shoulder work you asked for as posture: a loadable exercise, 15 lb so far, not a band.

exercises.name: BB Row
exercises.cue: Hinge forward until your chest is roughly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent, back flat. Breathe in and brace. Pull the bar to your belly button by driving your ELBOWS back past your ribs, then lower it all the way under control. Your torso does not move: if you are standing up a little to help the bar, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Lat Pulldown
alts.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight. Building toward real pull-ups.

alts.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
alts.cue: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.

alts.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
alts.cue: Chest on an incline bench, dumbbells hanging. The bench removes the lower back entirely, so nothing can cheat. Good on a day the RDLs left your back tired.

alts.name: Seated Cable Row
alts.cue: Tall chest, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, let it stretch all the way forward.

alts.name: DB Pullover
alts.cue: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

exercises.name: DB Reverse Fly
exercises.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand. Push your hips back and lean your chest forward to about 45 degrees, back flat, eyes down. Let the dumbbells hang below your chest with a small bend in the elbows. Open your arms out to the SIDES like opening curtains until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Your torso does not rise. Go light, this is a small muscle.

alts.name: Cable Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the adjustable cable column, standing tall, a handle in each hand and a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Same movement lying face down on an incline bench, which removes the lower back entirely. Use this if the standing version makes your back ache.

exercises.whyHere: they are the back-of-the-shoulder work you asked for as posture

blocks.label: Single leg, carries in the rest
blocks.why: The single-leg squat, second leg work of the day. The farmer carry rides in its rest: grip and trunk, nothing the split squat is using, and it is the carry you asked for on 15 August.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Lighter than the back squat on purpose. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Fingertips just hook under the bar; the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. Because the bar is in front, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier. If the elbows drop the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Cossack Squat
alts.cue: Feet wide, toes turned out a little, a light dumbbell held at your chest or nothing at all. Shift all your weight onto one leg and sit down over that heel as low as you can while the other leg stays straight, that foot rolling up onto its heel. Push back up and shift to the other side. Go only as low as your heel stays flat. THIS CUE IS A DRAFT: say what it should say.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: A heavy dumbbell in each hand. Stand as tall as you can, shoulders back, stomach tight, and walk for the seconds shown. Put them down before your form falls apart, not after. Start the watch before you pick them up, because both hands are full. Count seconds and type the seconds. Get to the top of the range on time first, then go heavier.

alts.name: DB Static Hold
alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: KB Farmer Carry
alts.cue: Kettlebells instead, and THE RACK STOPS AT 50 LB EACH: that is the whole set, 20 up to 50, two of each. His note #18, 2026-08-25: 'Therea no kettlebell after 50 for farmers'. He is right, and it is why the prescribed version is dumbbells, which go to 90 and which he has already carried at 75 per hand. Use this one when the dumbbells are taken, not when you want it heavier. They hang differently and swing a little, so the grip works harder at the same weight.

alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

exercises.whyHere: grip and trunk, nothing the split squat is using

blocks.label: Bound sideways
blocks.why: Three bounds of three each side, first, while you are fresh. Your own ask on 15 August: "all this lifting is just one plane. I am not doing side or whatever else." Inside the session rather than in one of its own, so it happens.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound

Land with the knee bent and pointing over the toes, never caving inward. Only jump as far as you can land and hold. Silent landing, no wobble, no second little hop. If you cannot freeze it, go shorter.

alts.name: Box Jump

Stand a forearm length from the box, swing the arms back, bend the knees a quarter of the way, and jump ONTO the box. Land with both feet flat and knees bent, quietly. STEP down, never jump down. A thud, or a third jump slower than the first, means the box is too high.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces on the balls of your feet, stiff ankles. 3x15.

alts.name: Banded Lateral Walk
alts.cue: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.

alts.name: Lateral Line Hop
alts.cue: The easier version. Both feet together, hop side to side over a line on the floor, small and fast, staying on the balls of your feet. 3x15.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Short band above the knees, seated on a bench. Push the knees apart against the band and hold two seconds at the widest point, then let them come back slowly. Success looks like: you feel it on the outside of the hip, above and behind the hip bone. 3x15.

blocks.label: Hinge, push-ups in the rest
blocks.why: The heavy hinge first, at your own rep range of six to eight. The push-ups ride in its three-minute rest on the floor beside the rack: your second chest exercise of the week, and a press uses nothing a deadlift does.

exercises.name: BB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: The heavy hinge. Breathe IN and tighten your stomach. Bar touches your legs the whole way, shins vertical. Bend the knees slightly and FREEZE them, then push your hips back toward the wall behind you. Go down until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height, and no further. Squeeze your bum and drive the hips forward to stand. If your lower back rounds you went too far. Straps are fine.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: KB Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.

alts.name: Smith RDL
alts.cue: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

alts.name: Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: One dumbbell, in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg. Stand on one leg with a soft knee, push the hips back and let the free leg travel straight back behind you as the dumbbell lowers down the standing shin. Stop when the hamstring of the standing leg pulls; do not chase the floor. Success: your hips stay level, no rolling open to the side. Hold the rack with your free hand if you wobble, that is not cheating. 8/leg.

exercises.name: Pushup
exercises.cue: On the floor beside the rack between deadlift sets. Hands a little wider than your shoulders, body one straight line from head to heels, bum and stomach squeezed before you lower. Chest to a fist off the floor, elbows going back at about 45 degrees, then push up. Success: hips and chest arrive at the top together. If the hips sag, do them with your hands on the bench instead.
exercises.whyHere: a press uses nothing a deadlift does

blocks.label: Press, curls in the rest
blocks.why: The overhead press, standing barbell in the rack, 5 lb steps, which is why it is the barbell and not the seated dumbbells that sat at 60 lb since May. The curls ride in its rest: the plain dumbbell curl you swapped to yourself, because the dumbbells travel to the rack and biceps do nothing in a press. Hammer and incline curls are one tap away.

exercises.name: BB Overhead Press
exercises.cue: Standing, bar in the rack at upper-chest height, grip just outside your shoulders. Squeeze your bum and tighten your stomach BEFORE you press, so your ribs do not flare and your lower back does not arch. Press straight up, moving your head back out of the way, until the arms lock out over the middle of your head. Lower under control. If your back arches to start the rep, go lighter.

alts.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: STANDING, not seated: that is the difference between this and the seated version in the alternatives, and it is why this needs no bench. Done second in the session from 2026-08-22, and the reason is in "Why this is here". Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward. Squeeze your bum and tighten your stomach BEFORE you press, so your ribs do not flare and your lower back does not arch. Press straight up until the arms are locked out with the dumbbells over the middle of your head, not in front of your face. Lower under control to the shoulders. Success looks like: your ribs stay down and you can hold the lockout still for a second. If your back arches to start the rep, go lighter.

alts.name: Machine Shoulder Press
alts.cue: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, not above your ears. Press up until your arms are straight without shrugging, and come back down slowly until the handles are level with your shoulders again. Stop the set when your lower back starts arching off the pad.

alts.name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Press
alts.cue: One knee down, the other foot forward, one dumbbell in the hand on the SAME side as the down knee. Press it straight overhead without letting your ribs flare or your body lean away. It is two exercises at once: a press, and your trunk refusing to bend sideways under a load held on one side. Lighter than the two-dumbbell version by a lot, and that is the point.

alts.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Bench upright, back supported. Takes the lower back out of it entirely.

exercises.name: DB Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Standing, dumbbells, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.

alts.name: DB Hammer Curl
alts.cue: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs the whole way, like holding two hammers. Curl both up together until the dumbbells reach shoulder height, elbows staying at your sides, then lower slowly. Your torso does not rock. If your elbows drift forward or your back leans, go lighter.

alts.name: Incline DB Curl
alts.cue: A dumbbell in each hand on the incline bench. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.

exercises.whyHere: biceps do nothing in a press

blocks.label: Front squat, dead bugs in the rest
blocks.why: The upright squat, lighter than Session A's heavy one, where depth comes easier. The dead bugs ride in its rest on the floor beside the rack: the trunk work for this session, so core is not all in Session A, and a squat uses nothing a dead bug does.

exercises.cue: Lighter than the back squat on purpose. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Fingertips just hook under the bar; the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. Because the bar is in front, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier. If the elbows drop the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.cue: The lift the week is built around. Stance a little wider than your hips, toes turned out slightly. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach as if about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep.

alts.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: On the floor beside the rack between front squat sets. On your back, arms straight up, knees bent over your hips. Press your lower back FLAT into the floor and keep it there: that is the whole exercise. Slowly lower one arm behind your head and the opposite leg toward the floor, breathing out. Stop the moment your lower back lifts. Swap sides. Your most-logged exercise: 21 sets in the last month.
exercises.whyHere: the trunk work for this session, so core is not all in Session A

blocks.label: Pull, triceps in the rest
blocks.why: The lat pulldown, at the pulldown station specifically (not the straight-arm station, which is a different column), last because the walk to the cables is one you make once. The dumbbell tricep extension rides in its rest because one dumbbell travels, and triceps do nothing in a pull. You have worked it at 42.5 to 50 lb.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight. Building toward real pull-ups.

alts.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
alts.cue: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

alts.name: DB Pullover
alts.cue: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.

exercises.name: DB Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.cue: One dumbbell held in both hands, straight above your head, elbows close to your ears. Lower it behind your head by bending only at the elbow, then press back up. Upper arms stay still and vertical the whole time. This one stretches the long head of the triceps where the pushdown shortens it, which is why they are not the same exercise. You have worked this at 42.5 to 50 lb.
